title: Types of reactions

match.reason: The new point is a broad overview of several reaction types, including combustion and acids reacting with metals or carbonates, and no bank point covers that set; the closest ones each teach only one type (decomposition, precipitation or displacement) or a different idea (rates, signs of reaction).

draft.title: Types of reactions
card: Combustion

a substance reacts with oxygen and gives off heat and light. Burning methane in a gas stove is an example. A complete combustion of a fuel containing carbon and hydrogen makes carbon dioxide and water.
Decomposition
one substance breaks down into two or more simpler substances. Heating calcium carbonate gives calcium oxide and carbon dioxide.
Precipitation
two solutions are mixed and an insoluble solid forms. The solid is called the precipitate. Mixing silver nitrate and sodium chloride solutions makes solid silver chloride.
Acid reactions
an acid reacting with a metal makes a salt and hydrogen gas. An acid reacting with a carbonate makes a salt, water and carbon dioxide gas.
draft.remember: Match the reaction to what you start with and what you see: oxygen and burning, one thing splitting, a solid forming from solutions, or an acid giving off gas.

a.q: Which reaction is a precipitation reaction?
opts: Two clear solutions mixed form a solid that sinks
A candle burns in air and gives off heat and light
A carbonate is heated and gives off a gas
A metal is added to acid and fizzes
a.why: Precipitation is when two solutions mix and an insoluble solid forms. The fizzing metal in acid makes hydrogen gas, so it is an acid reaction, not a precipitation.
a.clue: Look for two solutions making a solid.

b.q: Zara drops a piece of limestone, which is mostly calcium carbonate, into dilute hydrochloric acid. It fizzes and the gas turns limewater cloudy. Which type of reaction is this?
opts: An acid reacting with a carbonate
Decomposition by heating
Combustion in oxygen
Precipitation of an insoluble solid
b.why: A carbonate added to an acid fizzes as carbon dioxide gas is released, along with a salt and water. It is not decomposition, because nothing was heated and the acid takes part in the reaction.
b.clue: What two substances were mixed, and what gas formed?

a.best: Two clear solutions mixed form a solid that sinks

b.best: An acid reacting with a carbonate

problems.detail: The clue 'Look for two solutions making a solid' restates the right option almost word for word, so a student can pick it by matching words without knowing what precipitation is.
